{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZV5kKw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC9Nyg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 23, "title": "Restore DMA/HDMA A-bus reads of $4210–$421F and their register side effects", "body": "## Problem

Merge `e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923` introduced a DMA/HDMA regression: `dma_a_blocked` uses one read/write exclusion table that includes `$4210–$421F`. Consequently, transfers read zero instead of CPU status/result registers, `$4210/$4211` reads do not acknowledge their flags, and HDMA can mistake an accessible register-backed descriptor for a zero terminator.

This corrects the unsupported portion of Issue #21's contract. Passing its contract tests does not establish hardware correctness. The supplied context lists no open Issue duplicating this correction.

## Expected outcome

In system-I/O banks `$00–$3F/$80–$BF`, DMA/HDMA A-bus reads at `$4210–$421F` reach the existing register handlers:

| Address | Required behavior within this correction |
| --- | --- |
| `$4210` RDNMI | Return the NMI status and acknowledge its read-clear flag. |
| `$4211` TIMEUP | Return the IRQ status and acknowledge its read-clear flag. |
| `$4212` HVBJOY | Return current blanking/automatic-controller-read status. |
| `$4213` RDIO | Reach the existing I/O read handler. Full external-pin behavior remains outside scope. |
| `$4214–$4217` | Return completed division/multiplication results. |
| `$4218–$421F` | Reach the existing automatic-controller result handlers. This does not implement missing controller ports or data lines. |

Apply this access rule to general DMA, direct/indirect HDMA payloads, and HDMA descriptor/indirect-pointer fetches. Descriptor termination depends on the fetched byte being zero; accessible register addresses must not be forcibly converted into terminators. Reads retain register side effects even when the fetched byte is used as a descriptor or pointer.

Read accessibility must not enable writes to these read-only registers or remove established A-bus exclusions. Keep CPU and B-bus decoding intact, including legal B-bus activity when an A-bus operation is excluded.

### Specification basis and limits

The repository's [Issue #21 reference assessment](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/docs/issue-21-validation.md#contract-and-reference-limitations) records:

- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **Unpredictable Things → Open Bus for DMA**, explicitly identifies `$4210–$421F` as accessible and identifies `$2100–$21FF`, `$4000–$41FF`, and `$4300–$437F` as open-bus areas. Its register descriptions cover RDNMI/TIMEUP acknowledgement and status/result registers.
- [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), **DMA AND HDMA**, identifies excluded A-bus endpoints including B-bus ports and `$4300–$437F/$420B/$420C`; **43x0 DMAPx** describes HDMA direction.

These references were not independently fetched during this repository-only evaluation. The recorded assessment already contradicts Issue #21's blanket zero-read requirement. Before merge, document the precise reference sections supporting the corrected access and acknowledgement expectations. Do not present excluded-read zero values, floating bits, or retained timing conventions as independently verified hardware facts.

### Focused scope and non-goals

Implement this register-read correction and distinguish read/write policy where necessary. Preserve established exclusions and unaffected transfer behavior. Existing write restrictions elsewhere in `$4200–$420F` and excluded-read value approximations are not certified by this Issue and must remain explicitly unresolved where unsupported.

Separate work remains for exact electrical/open-bus values, WRAM–`$2180` conflicts, DMA startup/alignment, HDMA initialization/first-frame/overhead behavior, same-channel contention, and the full mode/channel/device-interaction matrix. No scheduler redesign, controller expansion, unrelated hardware feature, UI work, commercial ROM, or firmware acquisition is required.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant inspected code and tests:

- [machine.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L413): the shared filter blocks the entire `$4200–$421F` range; `transfer` and `hdma_read` use it. Existing handlers at lines 285–305 already provide status/result reads and acknowledgement.
- [dma_tests.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L115): several tests require pending NMI/IRQ to survive DMA/HDMA reads, including descriptor, payload, and pointer-fetch cases. Those expectations encode the regression.
- [dma_access.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/crates/snes-core/tests/dma_access.rs): original source-built guests provide a suitable integration-test pattern, but currently contain no positive status/result-read coverage.

Minimal reproduction: arrange a pending NMI flag, configure fixed-source general DMA from `$00:4210` to legal B-bus `$2180`, and transfer two bytes away from timing boundaries. Currently both bytes are zero and the NMI flag remains set. Expected transferred bit-7 values are `$80` then `$00`, and the flag is acknowledged. Mask floating bits rather than inventing an electrical bus-value requirement. Repeat for `$4211` and IRQ status.

Evaluation was read-only: no files changed, suites rerun, external sources fetched, or external actions performed.

Inventory continuity: all supplied category scopes and statuses remain unchanged. `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `dsp-voices` remains implemented_unverified; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster`, and `pal` remain unimplemented.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement accessible `$4210–$421F` A-bus reads through all named DMA/HDMA paths. Preserve read-only write behavior, established exclusions, bank decoding, legal B-bus activity, address/count progression, and unaffected timing behavior.
- [ ] Replace contradictory Issue #21 assertions with specification-derived original vectors. Preserve unrelated coverage. Demonstrate that newly added positive-read cases fail on baseline `e77cad3` and pass with the correction, without altering baseline production logic.
- [ ] Cover all sixteen register offsets, representative system-bank mirrors including `$00/$3F/$80/$BF`, and outside-I/O-bank controls including `$40/$C0` and WRAM. Cover fixed/incrementing/decrementing transfers across `$420F/$4210` and `$421F/$4220`, with final addresses/counts asserted.
- [ ] Test repeated `$4210/$4211` reads: first-read status, acknowledgement, second-read cleared status, and unrelated flag preservation. Preserve existing deferred-NMI coverage; acknowledging RDNMI must not accidentally discard an already queued NMI event.
- [ ] Test `$4212` at stable blanking/auto-read states using documented driven-bit masks. Verify literal arithmetic-result bytes and nonzero first-controller automatic results. Route remaining result registers through their existing model without claiming missing controller functionality verified.
- [ ] Exercise direct and indirect HDMA payload reads, accessible nonzero and zero descriptors, and both indirect-pointer bytes backed by accessible registers. Assert fetched values, acknowledgement, channel continuation/termination, and pointer progression. Retain excluded-endpoint side-effect controls and reverse-transfer B-bus progression.
- [ ] Add original source-built 65C816 guest coverage through `Machine` for positive DMA status/result reads and CPU-visible numeric WRAM results. Guest code performs initialization and transfer triggers; host code does not inject private flags or expected results. Use explicit instruction/frame deadlines and document MIT provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Run `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::dma_tests`, `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Preserve existing DMA access-boundary, HDMA preemption, deferred-NMI, CPU, PPU, SPC, and DSP regressions.
- [ ] Run the existing [README validation commands](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/README.md#validate) and [.github/workflows/ci.yml gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/e77cad3e5185959bb1c264d23833223215984923/.github/workflows/ci.yml): reproducible smoke fixture, pinned source-built CPU/SPC suites, licensed HDMA scanline fixture, twice-built cleared games, Wasm build, and `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Retain both 18,100-frame cleared-game replays, Castle's complete route/credits, Memory audio checks, freeze negative controls, SRAM recovery, and Pages subpath smoke. Do not shorten runs, weaken assertions, or change fixtures to hide failures.
- [ ] Update README and validation evidence to supersede the incorrect read contract, distinguish documented access rules from bus-value approximations, and report actual passes/failures/unperformed checks. Retain provenance requirements and outstanding DMA/HDMA limitations. Limited suite passes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
